[[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]] |} ===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)=== A total of 22 teams will contest the league, comprising 15 sides from the [[2025–26 Segunda División|2025–26 season]], three relegated from the [[2025–26 La Liga]], and four promoted from the [[2025–26 Primera Federación]]. ;Teams promoted to La Liga On 16 May 2026, [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]] became the first side to mathematically be promoted, following a 3–2 win against [[Real Valladolid]]; they secured a return to the top flight after a 14-year absence. [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] became the second team to be promoted, on the penultimate matchday after defeating Real Valladolid 2–0. The third and final team was [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], who secures the promotion spot by defeating Almería 2–1 on aggregate in the promotion play-offs. Both Deportivo and Málaga returned to La Liga after 8 years absence. ;Teams relegated from La Liga On 11 May 2026, [[Real Oviedo|Oviedo]] became the first team to be relegated to the second division, following a 1–1 draw between [[Rayo Vallecano]] and [[Girona CF|Girona]]. They returned after spending only one season in the Spanish top flight.{{Cite web |title=Girona Draw With Rayo Vallecano as Real Oviedo Suffer La Liga Relegation |url=https://dailypioneer.com/news/real-oviedo-relegated-from-la-liga |access-date=2026-05-13 |website=dailypioneer.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2026-05-12 |title=Real Oviedo first team relegated after Rayo Vallecano 1-1 Girona draw |url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/real-oviedo-first-team-relegated-after-rayo-vallecano-1-1-girona-draw-42857598 |access-date=2026-05-13 |website=OneFootball |language=en}} The second and third teams to be relegated were [[Girona FC|Girona]] and [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], both on 23 May 2026, ending their stints of four and five years in the top flight respectively. ;Teams relegated to Primera Federación The first, second, and third teams to be relegated were [[Real Zaragoza|Zaragoza]], [[Cultural y Deportiva Leonesa|Cultural Leonesa]], and [[SD Huesca|Huesca]], after they failed to win their respective matches on 24 May 2026. This ended Zaragoza's 77-year streak in professional football, having spent 55 of those seasons in La Liga. Cultural Leonesa returned to the third tier after only one season, and Huesca was relegated after spending 11 years in professional football. On 31 May 2026, [[CD Mirandés|Mirandés]] became the fourth and last team to be relegated to the third tier, after a seven-year stint in the second division. ;Teams promoted from Primera Federación On 1 May 2026, [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]] became the first team to achieve promotion to the second division, following a 2–0 win against [[Barakaldo CF|Barakaldo]]. They return after a one-year absence.{{Cite web |last=read |first=OneFootball·2 min |date=2026-05-01 |title=🚨Official: Tenerife return to LaLiga Hypermotion |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/official-tenerife-return-laliga-hypermotion-163300318.html |access-date=2026-05-13 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}} The second team to earn promotion was [[CD Eldense|Eldense]] following a 2–1 win against [[Atlético Madrileño]] on 16 May 2026, also returning at their first attempt. On 19 June 2026, The third team to secure promotion was [[CE Sabadell FC|Sabadell]] who returned after a five-year absence after beating [[Zamora CF|Zamora]] 4–1 on aggregate in the final promotion play-off. The last team to earn promotion was [[RC Celta Fortuna|Celta Fortuna]], the B team of [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]], entering the second tier for the first time in their club history after a victory
